title: Ops Launchpad: readiness sprint tracker and KPI ledger
body:
Purpose and scope:
A compact, single-sheet tracker intended for product-ops + release leads to run a 6-week readiness sprint for medium-impact feature launches (target: dedicated + hosted API changes). The sheet blends: (A) a rolling weekly runway with owners and hard blockers, (B) a canonical KPI ledger that ties to launch success criteria, and (C) a preflight checklist that gates rollout cadence (canary -> staged -> full).

How to use (quick):
- Scrum cadence: update by EOD Monday; product-ops consolidates for Tuesday go/no-go sync.
- Owners: put primary owner in OWNER column, escalation contact in ESCALATE.
- Score: each row has a R, A, G weekly status (red/amber/green) and a short rationale.
- KPIs: baseline, target at canary, target at full rollout. Post-launch cadence: daily for first 3 days, then twice-weekly until 4 weeks.

Top-level sections (sheet layout) — single sheet with named blocks:
1) Runway (columns): ID | AREA | TASK | OWNER | ESCALATE | DUE | WEEK(-4..+2) | STATUS(R/A/G) | NOTE | BLOCKER? | JIRA
Sample rows (CSV-ish):
ID,AREA,TASK,OWNER,ESCALATE,DUE,WEEK-2,WEEK-1,WEEK0,WEEK+1,STATUS,NOTE,BLOCKER?,JIRA
R1,infra,pre-provision dedicated pool,Marcus Chen,Liam O'Connor,2025-02-20,G,G,A,R,G,Waiting on quota,quota request pending,INFRA-112
R2,api,stable-rolling-deploy config,Jordan Rivera,Aisha Patel,2025-02-25,G,A,A,A,A,Canary flagged metrics,needs small config tweak,HOSTED-987
R3,docs,update SDK snippets,Priya Srinivasan,Jordan Rivera,2025-02-18,G,G,G,G,G,Minor wording differences,no,DOCS-21

Notes about runway rows: use short hand in NOTE (e.g., "perf ok @ 2k rps", "kv cache mismatch", "quant config pending"), use BLOCKER? flag only when deterministic.

2) KPI ledger (compact): one row per KPI with owner + baselines + targets + measurement query. Columns: KPI_ID | KPI_NAME | OWNER | BASELINE | CANARY_TARGET | FULL_TARGET | DATA_SOURCE | QUERY_LINK | SLI? | ALERT_THRESHOLD | POSTLAUNCH_FREQ
Sample KPI rows (CSV):
K1,median_latency_ms,prod-infra,28,30,35,Datadog,https://app.datadoghq.com/...,SLI,>100ms p99 alert,daily
K2,error_rate_pct,platform-team,0.03,0.05,0.1,Logs,https://logs.redwood/...,SLO,>0.5% sustained,real-time
K3,token_cost_usd_per_1k,finance,7.8,8.5,9.5,Billing,https://billing/reports/...,ops-metric,20% increase vs baseline,weekly

Important KPI guidance (ops):
- Keep the KPI set small (3–6) and map every KPI to a single OWNER.
- Mark whether a KPI is an SLI vs an internal metric for trade-offs.
- Define explicit alert thresholds and a recovery SLA (e.g., rollback within 60 min if p99 > 250ms for 30 min).

3) Preflight checklist (gating): rows are small pass/fail checks with owner + verification link + acceptable evidence. Columns: CHECK_ID | CHECK | OWNER | VERIFY_LINK | EVIDENCE_ACCEPTABLE | GATE (canary/staged/full) | STATUS
Sample checks (CSV):
C1,Canary traffic routing configured,Jordan Rivera,https://infra/route-config,traffic diverted to dedicated pool,canary,pass
C2,Fallback model variant tested,Aisha Patel,https://ci/pipelines/345,automated smoke with fallback,canary,pass
C3,Cost guardrails in billing dashboard,Finance,https://billing/gauges,alert + cap configured,staged,fail

Rollout gating rules (short):
- Canary: Requires 100% runway PASS for infra + API + rollback path; KPI canary targets must be defined (no missing queries).
- Staged: after 24–72h of canary with no critical alerts and KPI within canary thresholds.
- Full: 7–14 days post-staged with stable KPIs and no unmitigated blockers.

Canary plan (templated steps):
- Day 0 (deploy): enable canary routing (5% traffic) -> monitor latency, errors, cost -> snapshot telemetry at +30m, +2h, +6h.
- Escalation: if p99 latency > threshold for 30m or error_rate spike > 3x baseline -> immediate rollback and postmortem.
- Canary expansion: 5% -> 25% (24h) -> 50% (48h) -> staged (72h) with manual approval.

Risk register (brief):
- Risk: quantization regressions on rare prompts. Mitigation: add 12 prompt-led evals to nightly suite, owner: Applied ML.
- Risk: capacity quota delays. Mitigation: pre-request quota and reserve minimal burst pool; owner: Infra.
- Risk: billing surprises on embeddings use. Mitigation: enable hourly alert and per-route caps; owner: Finance.

Slack / Jira / Docs hygiene tips (notes-to-self):
- Create a single Slack thread per launch and pin the README and current sheet link.
- Link the KPI queries; avoid ad-hoc dashboards unless linkable.
- For each JIRA listed in the runway rows, add the sheet link to the ticket (makes traceability easier).

Open questions / TODO (live):
- Who will own the 24/7 on-call window in first 72h? (proposed: product-ops + infra rotation)
- Do we require conformance testing for the private deployment packaging for this launch? (ask Private Deployments team)
- Can Finance short-circuit the cost cap automatically or is manual intervention required?

Quick retrospective template (post-launch):
- Wins: three bullet points (what improved deploy runway or reduced toil).
- Misses: three bullet points (which blockers cost time).
- Action items: numbered list with owners and due dates (add back to runway rows R-xxxx).

Appendix: quick glossary
- Canary = small-percentage live traffic experiment.
- Staged = broader percentage with manual gating.
- SLI = service-level indicator (user-facing metric).
- KPI ledger = single source of truth for launch success metrics.

Evidence examples (what we accept as "pass"):
- Datadog dashboard snapshot URL with timestamp + query.
- CI run link showing smoke tests (exit code 0 and sample latencies).
- Billing snapshot showing cost per 1k tokens within agreed cadence.

Quick-change log (for sheet edits):
- 2025-02-12 Jordan R: initial seed (runway + KPIs + preflight template).
- 2025-02-20 Marcus C: added infra quota rows + escalation contact.
- 2025-03-01 Aisha P: updated KPI targets after benchmark run and flagged billing guardrail fail.

If you're using this sheet as a handoff artifact (engineering -> customer success -> support), please ensure the "NOTE" column includes: short summary, direct link to playbook, and a single escalation step (who to call).

Internal shorthand and common abbreviations used here:
- r = rollout, s = staged, c = canary, pb = private build, kv = key-value cache, q = quantize/quantization, tf = traffic fraction.

End of doc.
